newsitem.title: UK: New altimeter to save airlines millions of pounds.
newsitem.headline: New altimeter to save airlines millions of pounds.

text.p: Improvements to the accuracy of aircraft altimeters could save airlines up to 20 million pounds ($30 million) a year on cross-Atlantic flights by the year 2015, a British aviation body said on Thursday.

The National Air Traffic Services Ltd (NATS) said the improved altimeters meant the safe distance between aircraft flying above each other could be reduced to 1,000 feet (300 metres) from 2,000 feet (600 metres) and thus increase flights and fuel economy.
NATS has called the new air traffic control system the "reduced vertical separation minima" (RVSM).

"The introduction of the RVSM means there will now be additional flight levels available," said air traffic control manager Bob Thomson in a statement. "Ultimately it will also enable increases in capacity to meet future demand."
"More aircraft will be able to fly, for more of the time, at the heights that allow maximum fuel economy," Thomson said. "RVSM will result in fuel and time savings for the airlines."

As a plane burns up fuel and becomes lighter it is more efficient if it changes heights. The new flight levels created by the RVSM will allow more safe flight levels and thus bring improved fuel economy, the statement said.
Currently 70 percent of the planes that fly in the North Atlantic region are equipped to operate RVSM.
RVSM has been introduced initially at altitudes between 33,000 feet and 37,000 feet by all traffic control services in the region, including Britain, United States, Portugal, Canada and Iceland.
NATS said they hoped to widen the levels when a higher proportion of planes are RVSM capable. ($1=.6124 Pound)
